A Reform UK councillor has complained to Parliament about MP Sam Carling over a 199-home development between Ramsey and Bury. Cllr Karan Maheshwari, who represents Ramsey on Huntingdonshire District Council, has submitted a complaint to the Parliamentary Commissioner for Standards. It concerns North West Cambridgeshire MP Mr Carling’s response to Cllr Maheshwari’s request for him to intervene in planning application 25/01382/OUT, for 199 homes between Ramsey and Bury. A copy seen by this publication is dated November 2 and marked “DRAFT – NOT SUBMITTED”, but Cllr Maheshwari later confirmed he submitted it on November 3 and received confirmation on November 4. The dispute began after Huntingdonshire District Council’s development management committee said it was minded to reject the scheme. Cllr Maheshwari says he asked Mr Carling to urge the Secretary of State not to “call in” the application. A planning application being called in means the Government takes responsibility for deciding it instead of leaving the final decision with the local authority. rawItems.title: Refurbished five-bedroom Godmanchester property on sale for offers over £850,000
rawItems.content: A five-bedroom property in Godmanchester is up for sale at offers over £850,000. The link-detached house on Old Court Hall has been completely refurbished by the current owners. Selling agent Fine & Country said: "Blending period charm with stylish contemporary finishes, this impressive home extends to over 2,000 sq ft of versatile family accommodation and retains a wealth of original features that celebrate its rich heritage." Entering the property, the hallway leads to the open-plan family/dining room, the sitting room, the study and the cloakroom. The open-plan dining and family room combines exposed timber beams, original character features and a botanical feature wall (Image: Fine & Country) The family/dining room, which is 33ft long, has exposed timber beams, a brick fireplace with a wood-burning stove, bi-fold doors to the courtyard garden, and a feature wall which was spray painted by a local artist. The contemporary kitchen features an island and bi-fold doors opening to the landscaped courtyard garden (Image: Fine & Country) In the adjacent kitchen/breakfast room, there's bespoke cabinetry, an island, integrated appliances and bi-fold doors that open to outside. READ MORE: Cambridgeshire's best places to live 2026 On the first floor, the landing leads to three bedrooms and a four-piece family bathroom.
